An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
summary: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. No standard closed form is available for its remaining life expectancy, which must therefore be evaluated by numerical integration. We show that Siler remaining life expectancy at age $x$ is a Poisson mixture of Gompertz-Makeham remaining life expectancies, that is, a Poisson-weighted average of life expectancies in models with only a constant background hazard and an exponentially increasing senescence hazard. All components share the senescence hazard. Their background hazards increase from one component to the next by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines. The Poisson mean is the immaturity hazard that remains to be accumulated after age $x$. This representation yields an exact series of generalized exponential integrals with a closed-form bound on the truncation error. Replacing the background hazard by its discounted counterpart also gives the Laplace transform of the remaining lifetime. The mixture bounds the life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality: up to a term below the reciprocal of $a_2+b_1$, this loss equals the probability of an immaturity death times the life expectancy with the immaturity hazard removed. In annual Siler fits to Swedish female mortality, we estimate that the loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, which accounts for 15% of the gain in life expectancy at birth over the period.

title: Adaptation of breast cancer cells to serum-free defined medium reveals changes in proliferation, adhesion, and lipid metabolism
summary: Cancer cell metabolic dependencies are strongly influenced by nutrient availability, yet conventional culture conditions contain non-physiological nutrient concentrations and poorly defined serum components that may obscure metabolic vulnerabilities. Here, we investigated the adaptation of three breast cancer cell lines to physiologically relevant, serum-free defined medium (DM). Using a stepwise reduction in fetal bovine serum (FBS), we evaluated proliferation, adhesion, morphology, and transcriptional changes in HER2-positive SK-BR-3, triple-negative MDA-MB-231, and ER-positive/HER2-positive BT-474 cells. The three cell lines differed substantially in their ability to adapt to serum-free conditions. MDA-MB-231 cells adapted readily, maintaining proliferation and adhesion without exogenous substrate coatings. SK-BR-3 cells also achieved sustained proliferation in serum-free DM, but required a serum-derived coating to maintain adhesion. In contrast, BT-474 cells failed to sustain adhesion and proliferation following complete serum withdrawal, although they remained proliferative in medium containing 1% FBS. Adapted cells retained characteristic HER2 or vimentin expression despite changes in morphology and proliferation. RNA sequencing revealed extensive transcriptional remodeling, including reduced expression of cell-cycle-associated programs in SK-BR-3 cells and enrichment of cholesterol homeostasis gene sets in SK-BR-3 and MDA-MB-231 cells. Expression of cholesterol regulatory genes, including SREBF2, HMGCR, and LDLR, increased across all three lines. Together, these findings highlight cell-line-specific adhesion requirements and shared metabolic responses to serum withdrawal, establishing a framework for developing defined culture systems to investigate cancer metabolic dependencies through genetic screening.

title: The chloroplast-localised transporter RETICULATA controls palisade mesophyll cell division and expansion
summary: Plant leaves contain extensive intercellular air spaces, which contribute to photosynthetic capacity and water use efficiency in different environments. Despite this importance, the developmental mechanisms that control leaf air space patterning are poorly understood. For over 20 years it has been known that plants with disrupted chloroplast biogenesis and metabolism have increased intercellular air spaces, but the underlying molecular mechanism is unknown. Here, we characterise leaf air space morphogenesis in mutants of the chloroplast amino acid transporter RETICULATA (RE), which has enlarged air spaces. We show that the reticulata-6 (re-6) loss of function mutant exhibits increased air space expansion specifically in the palisade, and not the spongy, mesophyll. We also show that RE does not regulate air space patterning via programmed cell death, via a change in stomatal density or a change in cell identity of the mesophyll tissue. Instead, we quantify mesophyll cell morphology and division rates to show that RE acts by promoting early palisade cell division and suppressing later cell expansion. Overall, we show that RE specifically regulated palisade mesophyll morphogenesis and air space patterning and hypothesise that chloroplasts may act to regulate air space patterning in the palisade mesophyll in response to light.

title: Automated Segmentation of the Hypothalamus: Associations of Age and Socioeconomic Status with Subunit Volumes in Cognitively Healthy Adults
summary: Background: The hypothalamus regulates sleep-wake cycles, energy balance, and autonomic and neuroendocrine function, yet its small size and poorly contrasted boundaries have long hindered in vivo volumetry. Deep-learning segmentation now allows the hypothalamus to be divided into functionally meaningful subunits. We examined whether hypothalamic subunit volumes are associated with age and socioeconomic status (SES) in cognitively healthy adults. Methods: From the OASIS-1 cross-sectional dataset (n = 416, 18-96 years), 133 participants with a Clinical Dementia Rating of 0 and complete segmentation output were analysed (33-94 years). A FreeSurfer-based convolutional neural network, run on a cloud virtual machine, segmented five subunits per hemisphere. Volumes were normalised to estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV) and related to age and SES (Hollingshead index) using Pearson correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction; partial correlations adjusted for sex (age) and for age and sex (SES) served as sensitivity analyses. Results: Older age was associated with lower normalised volume of the right posterior subunit (r = -.456, q < .001) and the left posterior subunit (r = -.274, q = .007); both associations persisted after adjustment for sex. Lower SES showed a trend towards larger left anterior-inferior volume (r = .242, uncorrected p = .005) that did not survive FDR correction (q = .053). Conclusions: Age-related volumetric differences in the healthy hypothalamus appear to be concentrated in its posterior portion, a region housing arousal-promoting circuitry. Automated subunit segmentation offers a scalable tool for studying the hypothalamus in ageing and in relation to environmental exposures; the cross-sectional associations reported here should not be interpreted as causal or as within-person change.
